candidate_findings.message: test_send_request_to_llm never calls send_request_to_llm. It awaits the patched send_request_to_open_ai, whose side effect produces every value the test asserts, so the test cannot fail on a wrong implementation. Line 41 is `await chat_interface.send_request_to_open_ai(...)`, and line 24 patches that same name with an AsyncMock whose side_effect returns `("", [["Hello","Hi there!"]], "video_path.mp4")`. The real `send_request_to_llm` (chat/interface.py:77-94) builds the system prompt, joins on history, dispatches to elevenlabs or zonos, and appends to CHAT_HISTORY. None of that code runs.

The test needs pytest-mock and pytest-asyncio, and the project declares neither. pyproject.toml's dev group lists only `pytest` and `pytest-cov`. poetry.lock has no `name = "pytest-mock"` or `name = "pytest-asyncio"` package entry; those names appear only as other packages' extras. The test takes a `mocker` argument and is an `async def` marked `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.

The patch on _load_avatar_infos_for_chat does not reach the name imported at line 8, so the real loader runs against the real TinyDB at DB_PATH and fails when no settings row exists. Line 8 does `from aafactory.chat.interface import _load_avatar_infos_for_chat`, which binds the name locally before line 31 patches `aafactory.chat.interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat`, so the patch does not affect it. The real function (interface.py:55-60) runs `TinyDB(DB_PATH)` with DB_PATH = ROOT_DIR/databases/avatar_db.json (configuration.py:8), then `avatar_page_settings_table.get(doc_id=1).get("avatar_name")`, which raises on None in a fresh DB. tests/test_configuration.py defines a TEST_DB_PATH that this test does not use.

The mocks are never checked for calls, and the patched send_request_to_open_ai is called with ten positional arguments, while production calls it with a single messages list. There is no `assert_called*` anywhere in the file. The `send_request_to_generate_video` mock is never used. Line 41 calls `send_request_to_open_ai(avatar_info[9], "Hello", ...)` with 10 args, while interface.py:86 calls it as `send_request_to_open_ai(messages)`.

send_request_to_llm concatenates the previous user message onto the prompt, and leaves audio_response unbound when voice_model is unknown. Line 81 is `user_message = CHAT_HISTORY[-1][0] + user_prompt`, which joins only the last user text with no separator and drops assistant turns. Lines 87-91 assign `audio_response` only in the `elevenlabs`/`zonos` branches, then use it unconditionally. The new test mocks around send_request_to_llm and never exercises either path.

The test changes the module-global CHAT_HISTORY and never restores it, so state leaks into later tests. Line 14 calls `CHAT_HISTORY.clear()`, and then the side effect appends to the global list (line 21). There is no fixture teardown or monkeypatch of CHAT_HISTORY.

The User Guide still says notes are not saved and not undoable, but the change now saves them and makes them undoable. UserGuide.md:335 still reads "Records a date-bound note that will be persisted in future milestones. Currently, it validates syntax via CLI and confirms receipt." Line 360 still reads "`note` is not undoable yet because it currently validates input and shows a confirmation message without persisting data." The diff only changed the example on line 340. Meanwhile NoteCommand.execute now calls model.setNote and isStateMutating() returns true, and JsonSerializableAddressBook now writes the notes map to the data file.

AddressBook.removeNote has no caller outside tests, and the User Guide still advertises a `note d-/DATE` delete command that doesn't exist. AddressBook.removeNote(VisitDate) is new, but Model/ModelManager add only setNote and getPlannerNoteProperty. NoteCommandParser tokenizes only PREFIX_NAME and PREFIX_DATE and rejects input unless both are present. NoteCommand.MESSAGE_USAGE dropped the "Delete format: d-/DATE" line, but UserGuide.md:342-349 and the summary table at line 439 still advertise `note d-/2026-03-24`. Only AddressBookTest.removeNote_* calls the method.

setNotes/resetData wipes every note when given the address book's own live unmodifiable view. getNoteMap() returns Collections.unmodifiableMap(notes), a live view. Calling setNotes(book.getNoteMap()), resetData(book), or model.setAddressBook(model.getAddressBook()) reaches this.notes.clear() before putAll(notes), so the source map is already empty.

Recording a note on a date that already has one silently replaces it, and the message still says "New note recorded". NoteCommand.execute calls model.setNote(date, noteContent), and AddressBook.setNote calls notes.put(date, note), which overwrites any existing value. VisitDate subclasses compare by value (OneTimeDate.equals compares the LocalDate), so `d/2026-03-24` and `d/24/3/26` hit the same key. MESSAGE_SUCCESS is always "New note recorded: %1$s". `undo` can bring the old note back, but only one level of undo exists.

Notes are stored in a HashMap during serialization, so their order is lost on save and reload. `private final Map<String, String> notes = new HashMap<>();` collects the notes, and toModelType loops over notes.entrySet() to call addressBook.setNote. AddressBook keeps a LinkedHashMap, and ModelManager.updatePlannerNote joins notes in map order with "\n\n". The test updatePlannerNote_multipleNotes_mergesNotes comments "Use LinkedHashMap in AddressBook to ensure order", which shows the order was meant to be kept.

The planner joins a day's notes without saying which date rule each note came from. updatePlannerNote appends entry.getValue().toString() for every key where isOn(currentPlannedDate) is true, separated by "\n\n", wraps the result in a new NoteContent and shows it as one NoteCard. The VisitDate key is dropped. NoteContent.VALIDATION_REGEX was changed to "(?s)[^\\s].*" just so this joined text passes validation.

The tests miss undo/redo of notes, the planner panel listener and invalid notes in the data file, and one assertion is weak. setNote_updatesPlannerNote only checks `assertFalse(note.equals(initialPlannerNote))`; it would also pass if the initial value were some other non-null note. No test runs NoteCommand and then undoState/redoState, even though isStateMutating() is now true. No test covers the PlannerListPanel listener. JsonSerializableAddressBookTest adds no case for an invalid date key or a blank or null note value, so the new IllegalValueException branches in toModelType are untested.

The Rust benchmark never calls the converted function, so the reported Rust time and speedup measure an empty loop. _RUST_BENCH_TEMPLATE times a loop whose body is `// {fn_lower}({call_args});  // uncomment once the Rust signature is known` followed by `std::hint::black_box(&{first_array});`. run_benchmark then computes `speedup = fortran_ms / rust_ms` (line 326), and BenchResult.summary prints 'Rust is {ratio:.2f}x faster than Fortran'. That figure goes into the report and the CLI summary table.

The accuracy check reports a pass when no Rust-vs-Fortran comparison ran (crate build failed, no binary, or length mismatch). When `errors` is empty, run_accuracy_check returns `AccuracyResult(passed=fortran_ok_count > 0, ...)`, so a Fortran-only run counts as a pass. Line 676 also returns `passed=True` when no routine or source is given. convert.py and cli.py are called with `crate_dir if build_ok else None`, so a failed cargo build sends every function down this path. convert.py prints `"✅" if acc.passed` and reporter.py renders `✅` in the accuracy table.

For FUNCTIONs with array arguments (ddot, dasum, idamax…), the Fortran and Rust drivers print values in different orders, so the positional comparison lines up the wrong values. In generate_fortran_driver the array print loops are added first and the result is appended last (`print_lines.append(f"      WRITE(*,'{print_fmt}') {result_var}")`, line 471). _RUST_EXAMPLE_TEMPLATE_FN prints `_result` first and the arrays after (`println!("{{:.15e}}", _result as f64);` then `{rust_prints}`). Both outputs have the same length, so run_accuracy_check compares `rust_out[i]` against `fortran_out[i]` across shifted positions.

The default Hybrid f2c path copies C statements into the Rust body untranslated, so the output doesn't compile, yet the conversion is marked successful. _translate_c_line falls through to `return s + "  // TODO: verify"` for every C statement it does not recognise. f2c output such as `a_dim1 = *lda;` or `c__[i__ + j * c_dim1] = 0.;` is emitted verbatim inside `pub unsafe fn`, with i32/&mut [f64] parameters. convert() then sets `success=True` (line 100) without running any compile check, even though the module docstring promises 'Run cargo check and report results'. A single broken module fails `cargo build` for the whole crate.

Without f2c or an LLM key, the Hybrid fallback emits an empty stub body (source only as comments) and still reports conversion success. With f2c unavailable and no LLM key, convert calls _direct_fortran_to_rust, which emits the source only as comments and returns a constant for functions; convert unconditionally sets success=True. DGEMM therefore leaves C unchanged rather than computing alpha*A*B + beta*C.

The LLM strategies return success=True even when the code still fails to compile after the repair rounds; Agentic also replaces the checked source with an unchecked polish result. LLMFirstStrategy.convert returns `ConversionResult(..., success=True, ...)` whether or not the final `quick_check` passed; it only prints 'Could not fully compile…'. AgenticStrategy.convert does the same (agentic.py line 143) and then runs `polish_unsafe_rust` after the compile loop (line 135) without compiling again, so the final source was never checked.

An automatically found GitHub token (gh auth token / Copilot hosts.json) is sent as a Bearer header to any LLM_BASE_URL, which a .env file in the CWD can set. _resolve_api_key returns `_load_token_from_gh_cli()` / `_load_token_from_vscode_store()` for provider github_models (line 142). `self.base_url = base_url or os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL") or self._default_url()` is not restricted to the provider's endpoint. _load_dotenv and convert.py both load `.env` from the CWD, and chat() posts with `headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self.api_key}"`.

Fortran sources come from an unpinned `master` branch or over plain-HTTP fallbacks with no integrity check, and are then compiled, run and sent to the LLM. `_NETLIB_BASE = "http://www.netlib.org/blas/"`, `_BLAS_TARBALL = "http://www.netlib.org/blas/blas-3.11.0.tgz"`, and `_LAPACK_BLAS_GITHUB_RAW = ".../lapack/master/BLAS/SRC/"`, with no hash check. _compile_run_fortran and _run_fortran_bench compile and run the fetched files, and the strategies pass `routine.source` into the LLM prompts.

LLM-generated Rust is written into the crate, built and executed with the user's privileges, with no sandbox. scaffold_crate writes `r.rust_source` (the model's reply after _strip_fences) straight into `src/{mod}.rs`. build_crate, test_crate and _compile_run_rust_example then run `cargo build`/`cargo test` and execute the example binary with the user's privileges.

The tarball path-traversal guard ignores symlink and hardlink members, so a malicious tarball can still write outside output_dir. _try_download_tarball checks only that `(output_dir / member.name).resolve()` lies under output_dir, then calls `t.extractall(output_dir, members=safe_members)` with no `filter='data'` and no check of `member.issym()/islnk()` or `linkname`.

convert.py's .env loader keeps surrounding quotes and runs first, so a quoted LLM_API_KEY reaches the API with the quotes and authentication fails. At module import, convert.py does `os.environ.setdefault(_key.strip(), _val.strip())` with no quote stripping. llm_client._load_dotenv does strip quotes, but it skips any key already in os.environ (`if key and key not in os.environ`), so the quoted value wins.

Strategy 2's 'Questioner LLM' is a fixed list of keyword-triggered questions, not an LLM. _generate_questions builds `questions` from `if "LSAME" in routine.source.upper()`, `if "IMPLICIT" not in ...` and similar checks, with no LLM call. The README says 'Questioner LLM asks up to 3 clarifying questions'.

The Hybrid strategy uses the LLM polish output without stripping markdown fences, so a fenced reply produces an invalid .rs file. `polished = self.llm.polish_unsafe_rust(...)`; `if polished.strip(): rust_source = polished`. The other strategies pass the same call through `_strip_fences`.

The console_scripts entry point targets convert:main, but convert.py isn't packaged, so a non-editable install fails. The entry point targets convert:main, but setup declares only packages=find_packages() and no py_modules=['convert']; convert.py is a top-level module outside those packages. A wheel installation outside the checkout therefore lacks the entry point's target.

Routine headers with fixed-form continuation lines lose all their arguments. parse_source calls _extract_args on the first header line alone; _ARG_LIST requires the closing parenthesis on that line. Parsing `SUBROUTINE FOO(A,` followed by a fixed-form continuation `+ B)` reproduced args=[]. Subsequent hybrid conversion and driver generation use this empty list.

The README marks Milestone 1 (dgemm automated in all three strategies) as done and calls the output a 'ready-to-use crate'. `- [x] Milestone 1 — Automate dgemm conversion (all three strategies)`. Meanwhile the hybrid path emits uncompilable or TODO-stub bodies (`// TODO: translate from Fortran source`), and the Rust benchmark call is commented out.

About 3,000 lines of new pipeline code were added with no tests. The export contains no test files (no tests/ directory or test_*.py). README says `# Run the test suite (once tests are added)` / `# pytest`. The harness logic that decides pass/fail (run_accuracy_check, _fortran_call, parse_arg_declarations) has no unit coverage.

click, colorama and fparser are declared but never imported, and every dependency is unpinned. requirements.txt and setup.py list `click>=8.1.0`, `colorama>=0.4.6` and `fparser>=0.2.1`; grepping the package finds no import of click, colorama or fparser.

Rust is installed by piping an unpinned remote script to sh, and the toolchain updates on every container start. `RUN curl ... https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal`, and devcontainer.json has `"postStartCommand": "rustup update stable --no-self-update 2>/dev/null || true"`.

The 429 handling sleeps for whatever Retry-After the server sends, and if every attempt hits 429 the error message reads 'None'. `wait = int(resp.headers.get("Retry-After", "5")); time.sleep(wait); continue` has no cap. After all attempts end in 429, `last_exc` is still None in `raise LLMError(f"... {last_exc}")`.

generate_report opens a browser by default, including in --non-interactive mode. `open_browser: bool = True`, then `webbrowser.open(html_path.as_uri())`. convert.py's _run_non_interactive calls generate_report without passing `open_browser=False`.

The sample scope takes the first N Level-1 routines instead of the curated BLAS_SAMPLE, and several helpers are dead code. _parse_sample_input returns `BLAS_FUNCTIONS[:n]`. `BLAS_SAMPLE`, `topological_order`, `clippy_crate` and `add_rust_tests` are defined but never referenced.

The devcontainer and convert.py's docstring name 'copilot' as the default provider, while llm_client defaults to github_models. `"containerEnv": {"LLM_PROVIDER": "copilot"}` and convert.py's docstring has `LLM_PROVIDER copilot | openai | openai_compatible (default: copilot)`, whereas llm_client.py's default is `"github_models"` and treats copilot as a legacy alias.

On the GET download routes (consumer and publisher preview), the download_language query value isn't validated and now reaches the backend as both the Accept-Language header and the lang query parameter. On GET, `download_language = (req.query.download_language?.toString() || req.language) as Locale` is cast but never checked; `downloadLanguageValidator()` only runs in the POST branch. Before this change `fetch` overwrote it with `queryParams.set('lang', this.lang)`. Now `downloadPublishedData`/`downloadPublishedPivotData` pass `lang: language as Locale` (consumer-api.ts:228/241), and fetch puts it in `'Accept-Language': lang` and `queryParams.set('lang', lang)`. For example, `?download_language=xx` is forwarded to the backend as is, and a value with characters that aren't valid in a header makes `fetch` throw. That error gets wrapped as UnknownException.

`language as Locale` hides a type mismatch, because the parameter is still typed `string`. `downloadPublishedData(..., language: string)` followed by `lang: language as Locale`. The same pattern appears at consumer-api.ts:241 and publisher-api.ts:932. The callers already hold a `Locale`-typed value, so the parameter could be typed `Locale` without any cast.

The only new e2e test covers just the consumer, unfiltered, non-pivot CSV. Pivot downloads and the publisher preview download have no test. The new `CSV Download Language Content` test submits only `viewType: 'unfiltered'` (no pivot axes), so it exercises `downloadPublishedData` only. Nothing exercises `downloadPublishedPivotData` or `PublisherApi.downloadDatasetPreview`, both of which this diff changed.

No unit test checks that the download request carries the download language rather than the UI language. tests/publisher-api.test.ts asserts exact fetch URLs ending in `lang=en` for other methods, but there is no case for `downloadDatasetPreview`, and no consumer-api unit test for `downloadPublishedData` with `cy-GB` on an English-UI client. The only new test is the Playwright spec, which relies on the e2e fixture's `' - CY'` suffix (tests-e2e/publish/helpers/publishing-steps.ts:336).

'Not applicable' branches use `break` instead of `continue`, so the first such record ends the whole `for record in data` loop and every later record is silently dropped. `break` sits directly inside `for record in data:` (line 135) at lines 413 (Allosteric modulator, Action 'Neutral' or None), 530 (Antagonist, 'Partial agonist'), 710 (Fusion protein, 'Binding'), 925 (Type None, 'Binding'/'Competitive') and 1063 (Subunit-specific, 'Mixed'). The function then reaches `return [KnowledgeGraph(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)]` (line 1094) holding only the records processed so far. Each case only does `print("not applicable")` (stdout, not koza.log), so nothing records the truncation.

The action allowlists spell 'Agnoist', so Agonist/Agonist and Allosteric modulator/Agonist records emit no edges, and Activator/Agonist records fall to a fallback that sets no agonism mechanism and emits no physical-interaction edge. `agnoist_list_with_separate_directly_physically_interacts_with_edge = ['Activation', 'Agnoist', ...]` (line 257). The `elif record["Action"] == "Agonist"` arm inside that block can never be reached. The diff deleted the old `if record["Type"] == 'Agonist' and record["Action"] != "Binding"` fallback and added no `not in` branch for Agonist, so these records hit no branch. The same misspelling at line 331 drops Allosteric modulator/'Agonist' records.

Types that used to map every action now silently emit nothing for any action missing from their new allowlist. Before the change, `if record["Type"] == 'Antagonist' and record["Action"] != "Binding"`, `if record["Type"] == 'Antibody':`, `if record["Type"] == 'Channel blocker':` and `if record["Type"] == 'Gating inhibitor':` covered all actions. Now each is gated by `record["Action"] in <type>_list...` (lines 476, 571, 639, 699, 757) and has no `not in` counterpart.

`predicate` now defaults to the string "None", so Type-None and Subunit-specific fallback records whose action has no arm get an association with predicate "None". Line 138 sets `predicate = "None"`. The diff removed the old per-type `predicate = BIOLINK_AFFECTS` from the Type-None and Subunit-specific blocks. In the fallback at line 1059, an Action other than 'Mixed' or 'Potentiation' (for example None) leaves predicate as "None" when line 1076 passes it as `predicate = predicate`. The Type-None fallback (lines 966 onward) has the same gap for actions other than None and 'Potentiation'.

The Endogenous check matches only the exact string "TRUE", so other encodings silently keep affects/increased. `if record["Endogenous"] == "TRUE":` (line 159), with no normalisation of the value anywhere in prepare() or the transform. Nothing in the repo (yaml or tests) records what form the value takes in the CSV.

The groupby on Type/Action/Endogenous uses the default dropna=True, so rows with missing keys disappear before the transform. `source_subset_df.groupby(group_cols, as_index=False)` with `group_cols = ['Target', 'Target UniProt ID', 'Ligand ID', 'Ligand', 'Type', 'Action', 'Endogenous']` and no `dropna=False`. The transform still branches on `record["Action"] is None` and `record["Type"] is None` (for example lines 224 and 920).

Fusion protein/Inhibition records are now tagged molecular_channel_blockage instead of inhibition. Line 699 onward first sets `causal_mechanism_qualifier = CausalMechanismQualifierEnum.inhibition`, then the 'Inhibition' arm overrides it with `CausalMechanismQualifierEnum.molecular_channel_blockage` (line 712). Before the change, this path used `inhibition`.

The change rewrites every Type/Action mapping and adds aggregation and the Endogenous switch, with no tests. A search of tests/ for 'gtopdb' matches only tests/unit/ingests/dgidb/test_dgidb.py. The diff touches only gtopdb.py and gtopdb_rig.yaml.

The rig's identifier-type rename is partial: SmallMolecule still says 'GTOPDBLigand ID'. The diff changes the MolecularMixture entry to `"GTOPDB Ligand ID"`, but line 177 under `node_category: biolink:SmallMolecule` still reads `- "GTOPDBLigand ID"`.

The diff leaves commented-out code: an import, a log call and an assignment. `# Gene,` (line 14), `# koza.log(f"DataFrame columns: ...")` (line 91) and `# current_predicate_mapping = BIOLINK_AFFECTS` (line 163).

Every Type block repeats near-identical association construction with per-action if/elif ladders. A table-driven mapping would remove the duplication that produced the typos. Near-identical association_1/association_2 construction and append blocks appear in the Activator, Agonist, Allosteric modulator, Antagonist, Antibody, Channel blocker, Fusion protein, Gating inhibitor, Inhibitor, None and Subunit-specific branches. A single (Type, Action) → (mechanism, direction index) table would replace about 900 lines.

The yaml-language-server schema headers sit in double-quoted PowerShell strings, so `$schema` expands to an empty variable. Each manifest gets `# yaml-language-server: =https://...` instead of the schema reference. Lines 209, 222 and 243 are `@("# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://aka.ms/winget-manifest.version.1.12.0.schema.json", ...` in a `shell: pwsh` step. In an expandable (double-quoted) string `$schema` is a variable reference that ends at `=`, and nothing assigns `$schema`. The text therefore never contains `$schema=`. The comment at lines 201-204 says the pipeline 'fails manifest validation' without this header, so every 'Submit to winget' run still uploads manifests that fail. A single-quoted string or an escaped `` `$schema `` is needed.

The publish triggers are narrowed to source-file extensions and the workflow self-paths are removed. Merged PRs that change only versions, manifests, fonts, project files or the workflow files no longer publish. In the diff, `FIGLet.Python/**` became `FIGLet.Python/**/*.py`. Likewise `FIGLet/**` became `FIGLet/**/*.cs`, `FIGLet.TS/**` became `*.ts`/`*.tsx` only, `FIGPrint/**` became `*.cs`, and the VS and VS Code extension paths changed the same way. Every `.github/workflows/publish-*.yml` self-path was removed. publish-figlet-py.yml line 38 reads the major.minor base version from `pyproject.toml`, so a merged PR that only bumps it (or changes `fonts/small.flf`) no longer runs the publish job. The same goes for `FIGLet.TS/package.json`, `*.csproj`, `.vsixmanifest`/`.xaml` and the extension's `package.json`. Changes to the workflow files themselves, including this one's fixes to publish-figprint.yml, also wait for an unrelated `.cs` change to run. The only fallback is a manual `workflow_dispatch`.

insertBanner no longer replaces a non-empty selection. It always inserts at column 0 of the active line, so the selected text stays in the document. The diff removes `if (editor.selection.isEmpty) { editBuilder.insert(...) } else { editBuilder.replace(editor.selection, ...) }` and keeps only `editBuilder.insert(position, indentedBanner + '\n')`, where `position = currentPosition.with(currentPosition.line, 0)` and `currentPosition = editor.selection.active` (the selection's active end). None of the ChangeLog-2026.md entries in the diff mention this change.

The installer manifest drops `PortableCommandAlias: figprint`, but the changelog says the alias is defined. The removed manifest had `"  PortableCommandAlias: figprint",`. The new NestedInstallerFiles entries (lines 253-254 and 261-262) list only `- RelativeFilePath: FIGPrint.exe`. ChangeLog-2026.md says: 'Define `FIGPrint.exe` as the nested installer file with `figprint` as the portable command alias'.

The new enum member `BATCHFile` doesn't follow PascalCase and doesn't match the `BatchFile` name in the changelog. The enum adds `BATCHFile` next to `Bash` and the others. The static property is `LanguageCommentStyles.BatchFile = new CommentStyleInfo(CommentStyle.BATCHFile)`. ChangeLog-2026.md says 'Introduce `BatchFile` to `CommentStyle` enum'.

`$PackageId` is assigned again at line 193, duplicating `$packageId` from line 152. Line 152 has `$packageId  = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"` and line 193 has `$PackageId = "ByteForge.FIGPrint"`. Both spellings are then used: `$PackageId` in the manifests, `$packageId` in the upload message and PR title.

The length and flag caps do not prevent ReDoS. A short pattern with catastrophic backtracking passes validation and blocks the event loop when it runs. The only new runtime guard is `if (pattern.pattern.length > MAX_PATTERN_LENGTH)` before `new RegExp(pattern.pattern, safeFlags)` and `regex.exec(line)`. There is no timeout, no check for nested quantifiers, no worker isolation and no per-line length limit. Trigger: `add_custom_rule` with pattern `(a+)+$` (6 chars) gets through `validatePattern`, because it compiles and is under 1 000 chars. Then `execute_custom_rules` with code `'a'.repeat(40)+'!'` (far under 500 000) makes `regex.exec` backtrack exponentially. Even so, CHANGELOG.md line 36 says the caps are "preventing ReDoS attacks (#127)".

The size guard never checks that the path is a regular file. A device or FIFO reports size 0, passes the guard, and is then read with no limit. `getFileStats` calls `fs.promises.stat(filePath)` (fileUtils.ts:157), and the handler checks only `stats.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES` before `code = await readFile(path)`, which is `fs.promises.readFile(filePath, 'utf-8')` with no length limit. Trigger: `execute_custom_rules` with `path: '/dev/zero'`. `fileExists` passes, `stats.size` is 0, the guard passes, and `readFile` never reaches EOF. There is no `stats.isFile()` check, and the file can also grow between the stat and the read (TOCTOU).

validate_custom_pattern never checks flags, but the CHANGELOG says both tools enforce the flag allowlist. `handleValidateCustomPattern` builds `customPattern` without a `flags` field, and `parseValidateCustomPatternInput` (inputParser.ts:416-427) does not parse `flags`. So the `ALLOWED_FLAGS_RE` branch in `validatePattern` can never fire for this tool. CHANGELOG.md says "user-supplied regex patterns in `add_custom_rule` and `validate_custom_pattern` are now validated for length (≤1 000 chars) and flag allowlist".

The flag strip/dedupe/default logic appears twice, so validation and execution can drift apart. `pattern.flags.replace(/[^gimsuy]/g, '')`, `Array.from(new Set(stripped.split(''))).join('')` and the `'g'` fallback appear once in `executePattern` (lines 148-152) and again in `validatePattern` (lines 266-270). There is no shared helper.

The allowlist rejects the valid `d` and `v` flags and silently strips them at execution, which changes behaviour. `const ALLOWED_FLAGS_RE = /^[gimsuy]*$/;` makes `validatePattern` reject `flags: 'gd'` or `'v'`, which the old code (`new RegExp(pattern.pattern, pattern.flags || 'g')`) accepted. `executePattern` drops them with `replace(/[^gimsuy]/g, '')`.

The new handler tests don't show that the guard runs before the read, or that an accepted file is actually processed. The oversize test asserts only `.rejects.toThrow(McpError)` and never asserts that the mocked `readFile` was not called, so 'before reading' is untested. The boundary test asserts only `.resolves.toBeDefined()`. Also, `setRequestHandler`'s capture condition `schema?.method === 'tools/call' || typeof handler === 'function'` matches every call, so the handler is really chosen by the 'last call' lookup in `beforeEach`.

Each Pull/Push menu action or key binding starts an unguarded new thread, so overlapping syncs run concurrently against the same .local and repository files and can overwrite or corrupt state. Each worker does readLocalRepository → projectToLocalRepository → readRemoteRepository → writeLocalRepository/writeRemoteRepository on the same `${options.repository}` and `.local` files (`File(...).writer()` truncates on open). For example: press ctrl+\ twice, or press ctrl+shift+\ while `dialogConflictResolver` blocks the first worker in `invokeAndWait`. The two threads interleave reads and writes, and one overwrites the other's merged version vectors, or one reads a half-written file and hits the "corrupt. Requires manual fixing" path.

Sync snapshots the project's renames and comments on the worker thread, then later replaces the whole lists, so edits the user makes during the sync are silently lost. `projectToLocalRepository` (called at lines 550 and 589) reads `context!!.args.codeData.renames/comments` on the background thread while the GUI can still change them. The merged state is written to disk (`writeLocalRepository`) and only afterwards applied in `uiRun { localRepositoryToProject(localRepository) ... }` (lines 572-575, 645-648). `localRepositoryToProject` calls `setProjectRenames(newProjectRenames)`, which replaces the whole list. A rename made while the pre-pull script runs, or while the conflict dialog is open, is therefore lost from the project and was never recorded in the `.local` file. Unsynchronised cross-thread access to the JadxCodeData lists is also a data race.

An uncaught exception in the new worker thread ends Pull/Push silently, with no dialog. `kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() }` installs no try/catch and no uncaught-exception handler. Code reached from pull/push can throw: `context!!`, `localRepository!!`, `oldLocalRepositoryItem!!`, `newProjectItem!!`, `ProcessBuilder(command).start()` in `runScript` (throws IOException for a bad script path) and `process.waitFor()`. Before the change, these ran inside guiContext.uiRun on the EDT, where the host application's EDT exception handling applied. Now they go to the default thread handler, which only logs to stderr.

traceCallback sets context.result to the raw callback argument: the full Client for pool.connect, and the full Result with rows for a query before enrichedCb overwrites it. TracingChannel.traceCallback assigns the callback's second argument to context.result before publishing asyncStart. For pool.connect(), that argument is the full Client, and enrichedCb never replaces context.result; a Node 22 reproduction confirmed asyncEnd receives the Client instance. Client contains connectionParameters and password. The same pattern in packages/pg/lib/client.js:726 exposes the full query Result, including rows, to asyncStart before enrichedCb replaces it with command and rowCount.

With tracing on, the query callback no longer gets the Query as `this`. Query.handleReadyForQuery and Query.handleError invoke callbacks as this.callback(...), preserving the Query receiver. The tracing wrapper receives that receiver, but enrichedCb is an arrow function and invokes origCb(err, res) as a plain function, discarding it. Thus the same callback receives the Query without tracing and undefined as this in strict mode when tracing is subscribed.

Queries rejected because the client is not queryable or is ending are never traced. The `!this._queryable` and `this._ending` branches (lines 689-701) return before the `shouldTrace(queryChannel)` block at line 709. They call `query.handleError` on the original, unwrapped callback.

Multi-statement queries publish undefined rowCount and command. query.js line 142 calls `this.callback(null, this._results)`, and `_results` can be an array for multi-statement text. enrichedCb reads `res.rowCount` / `res.command` without checking for an array.

When a checkpoint exists but fails to load, training is skipped and p-values come from a freshly initialised, untrained model. The bad checkpoint is never overwritten. `load_model` catches every exception and returns `(None, None)`. Trigger: run once with the default out_dir (model.pt is saved), then rerun with input whose protein count differs after filtering. `load_state_dict` raises a size mismatch, the error is swallowed, and results come from the untrained model. A second trigger is `init_pca=False`: the saved encoder has no bias, but `load_model` builds with `prot_means=None`, so the encoder has a bias, the strict load fails, and the same path runs on every rerun.

`protrider plot encoding_dim` fails after a grid-search run: the file it reads is no longer written, and its column names changed. The diff removes `df_gs.to_csv(f'{out_dir}/grid_search.csv')` from `find_latent_dim`. The new `GridSearchResult.to_csv` writes `grid_search_results.csv` with columns `enc_dim`/`auprc`. `plot_encoding_dim` still runs `pd.read_csv(output_dir + "/grid_search.csv")` and uses the `encod_dim`/`aucpr` columns, so it raises FileNotFoundError on new output.

A previous run's checkpoint is reused silently whenever tensor shapes match, even if the input data, protein order or model settings changed. Outlier calls can then come from a model trained on different data. Checkpointing is on by default (`checkpoint_path = Path(config.out_dir) / 'model.pt'`). The checkpoint stores only `q`, `n_layers` and `presence_absence`. `find_q_method`, `lr`, `n_epochs`, `cov_used`, `init_pca` and the input file are not compared, and `h_dim` is taken from the current config. Training is skipped whenever loading succeeds, so rerunning with new samples or settings into the same out_dir reuses the stale model.

A model trained with init_pca=False cannot be restored from its checkpoint. init_model passes dataset.prot_means_torch when init_wPCA is false. ConditionalEnDecoder consequently subtracts these means and creates an encoder without bias. save_model does not preserve prot_means, while load_model always constructs with prot_means=None, creating an encoder bias and removing centering. load_state_dict therefore rejects the missing bias key for these saved models.

In grid or binary search, a non-finite training loss crashes the search with UnboundLocalError instead of skipping that q. In `train_and_eval_q`, the `if ~np.isfinite(loss):` branch assigns `auc_prec_rec = np.nan`, but the function returns `auprc`, which is only assigned in the else branch. The result is UnboundLocalError. The old loop simply did not append that q.

The binary search ('bs') logic is wrong: after a shrink step it always runs a shift step too, k_max and tol are never used, and points evaluated in the last iteration are never compared for best_q. The `if fM >= fL and fM >= fR:` shrink block is followed by an unconditional `if fR > fM: ... else: ...` rather than `elif`, so each iteration both shrinks and shifts. `k_max = injected_dataset.X.shape[1]` and `tol` are computed but never used, and `R = int(q * 3)` can exceed the number of samples or proteins. `best_q` is updated only at the top of each iteration, so points evaluated in the last iteration are recorded in `enc2auprc` but never compared. The loop variable `q` also shadows the outer `q`.

With common_degrees_freedom=False, the fallback df depends on protein order, because it is recomputed from a running median. Inside `for j, _mu, _sigma, _df in results:`, `df0` is recomputed from `np.nanmedian(df)` over the entries filled so far. The first 10 proteins always fall back to 10, later ones get a running median, and this costs O(n²) work. When the first-pass df exceeded `max_df` (set to NaN), `mu[j]`/`sigma[j]` keep the jointly fitted values from the huge df, but `df[j]` is set to `df0` without refitting.

PKCE is optional: an /authorize request without code_challenge yields a code that /token redeems for the GitHub token with no verifier and no client authentication. Authorize only checks the method `if codeChallenge != "" && codeChallengeMethod != "S256"`, so an empty challenge passes. ExchangeCode in session.go skips verification with `if sess.CodeChallenge != "" { verifyPKCE(...) }`. Token never checks client_id or a client secret. Anyone holding the internal code and redirect_uri gets the GitHub access_token back.

The client-supplied state is the session key and SaveSession overwrites any existing entry, so a second /authorize with the same state replaces an in-flight flow's redirect_uri and code_challenge. SaveSession does `s.sessions[state] = &Session{...}` with no check for an existing entry. Callback then looks up only by `state` (HasSession and CompleteCallback) and redirects to whatever `sess.RedirectURI` the most recent /authorize stored. Nothing binds the browser that started /authorize to the one that hits /callback (no cookie or server-generated nonce).

A second successful /callback for the same state mints another internal code without revoking the first. Both codes point at the shared Session, so the leftover code stays redeemable and can return a different (latest) access token. CompleteCallback assigns a new `code` and `s.codes[code] = sess` on every call, without removing an earlier sess.InternalCode. ExchangeCode does `delete(s.codes, code); delete(s.sessions, sess.State)`, but any other entries in s.codes still point to the same *Session, whose ExpiresAt is unchanged and whose AccessToken is still set.

Unauthenticated /authorize stores a session for every distinct state with no cap, so the map can grow without bound for the session TTL and exhaust the 256M container. Authorize sits on the public mux (`mux.HandleFunc("GET /authorize", ...)` in main.go). Each valid request calls `h.store.SaveSession(state, ...)` into an unbounded map, and the janitor only clears entries after ExpiresAt. The port is bound to 127.0.0.1, which limits who can reach it but does not bound the map.

If the user denies consent or GitHub returns error=, Callback answers with a bare 400 instead of redirecting the error to the client's redirect_uri, so the client's login hangs. Callback reads only `code` and `state` and returns `http.Error(w, "missing code or state", http.StatusBadRequest)` when code is empty. GitHub's `error`/`error_description` query parameters are never read or forwarded to sess.RedirectURI.

ValidateToken returns early on `h.store.LookupToken(token)` without contacting GitHub. middleware.Auth accepts any token for which ValidateToken returns a login, and there is no user allowlist or token-origin check.

A short JFIF APP0 segment makes FastImage.resolution raise NoMethodError even with raise_on_failure false. `data = @stream.read(length)` uses the segment's declared length. Once `data[0, 5] == "JFIF\0"` matches, `data[7].ord` and `data[8, 4].unpack("nn")` run with no length check. A declared length of 7 to 11 bytes makes `data[7]` or the slice nil, so the call raises NoMethodError. `fetch` (fastimage.rb:293-298) only rescues the listed fetch/parse errors (CannotParseImage, EOFError, etc.), so NoMethodError reaches the user. A length field under 2 makes `read(-n)` return nil, and `data[0,5]` raises the same way.

TIFF/EXIF X/YResolution rationals stored before the current stream position, or sharing one offset, are silently dropped, so resolution comes back nil. `read_rational_resolution` computes `skip_amount = absolute_pos - @stream.pos` and does `next if skip_amount < 0`. The stream only moves forward, so any rational offset before the current position is skipped without a value. Nothing records or reports this, and no fixture covers that layout ("test.dng" is expected to be nil without explanation).

Keyword-argument syntax (Ruby 2.0) and safe navigation (Ruby 2.3) break loading on older Rubies that the gemspec still allows. fastimage.gemspec declares required_ruby_version >= 1.9.2, but Exif#initialize now uses keyword-argument syntax requiring Ruby 2.0, and jpeg.rb:51 uses safe navigation requiring Ruby 2.3. lib/fastimage/fastimage.rb unconditionally requires both parsers, so requiring fastimage on those older permitted runtimes fails with SyntaxError before any API can run.

JFIF density always beats EXIF X/YResolution, so a JFIF 0-units 1:1 placeholder hides a real EXIF DPI. In the `MARKER_APP0` branch, `return [[x_density, y_density], unit_sym]` runs for any JFIF segment, including `JFIF_UNIT_ASPECT_RATIO` (mapped to :no_units). APP0 normally comes before APP1, so `exif_resolution` is never consulted. The locked fixture expects `"test3.jpg"=>[..., [[1, 1], :no_units]]`, so this precedence is never tested against a file that has both.

When there is no resolution, @resolution is never set, so every later resolution/resolution_units call fetches the image again. `parse_resolution` returning nil makes `parse_packets` raise CannotParseImage, which `fetch` swallows, so `@resolution` stays undefined. `resolution_units` then does `resolution unless defined?(@resolution)`, which calls `fetch` again. `test_instance_resolution_returns_nil_for_format_without_resolution` calls both on test.png and so fetches it twice, but passes.

The docs say resolution returns nil when the image has no resolution data, but with raise_on_failure: true it raises CannotParseImage. `ImageBase#resolution` returns nil, so `parse_packets` does `raise CannotParseImage`, and `fetch` re-raises it with `raise if @options[:raise_on_failure]`. The comment says "Returns nil if the image does not contain resolution information". No test exercises resolution with raise_on_failure.

Resolution values are Floats for EXIF/TIFF and Integers for JFIF/PNG/BMP, and the tests can't tell the difference. Exif uses `num.to_f / den`, while JFIF uses `unpack("nn")` and PNG uses `unpack("NN")`. The fixtures mix `[[72, 72], :inches]` (test.jpg) and `[[72.0, 72.0], :inches]` (test2.jpg), and `assert_equal` passes either way, so the test doesn't pin the type.

The centimeters, EXIF no-units, BMP one-zero-axis and JPEG EXIF-only branches have no tests. The resolution expectations in GoodFixtures contain only :inches, :meters and :no_units (from JFIF and PNG). No fixture produces :centimeters, so the `JFIF_UNIT_CENTIMETERS` and `RESOLUTION_UNIT_CENTIMETERS` branches in jpeg.rb and tiff.rb are never run.
BMP pixels-per-metre values are read as signed and are rejected only when both are zero. `x_ppm, y_ppm = data[38, 8].unpack("l<l<")` followed by `return nil if x_ppm == 0 && y_ppm == 0`.

Before setup is complete, any GitHub/Google OAuth user becomes ADMIN and setup gets finalized, so a stranger can take over a fresh install. The new `canSelfSignup` returns `{ allowed: true, role: Role.ADMIN }` whenever `emdash:setup_complete` is not true, before the allowed-domain check runs. After `handleOAuthCallback` it calls `finalizeSetup(emdash.db)`, which sets `emdash:setup_complete`. `/_emdash/api/auth/oauth/` is in PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES, and nothing links the callback to the setup wizard. Trigger: on a new install with GitHub OAuth configured, an attacker opens /_emdash/api/auth/oauth/github and finishes the GitHub login. They become admin and setup is marked complete. Before this change, the domain allowlist gated signup at this point.

Before setup is complete, whichever atproto DID finishes OAuth first becomes ADMIN with the owner's wizard email. The handle the owner entered is never checked. `isFirstUser = setupComplete !== true && setupComplete !== "true"`, and then `findOrCreateOAuthUser(..., async () => { if (isFirstUser) return { allowed: true, role: Role.ADMIN }; ...})`. setup-admin.ts stores `handle: body.handle` in setup_state, but callback.ts never compares it with `atprotoSession.did`. For the first user it sets `email = setupState?.email` and `emailVerified: isFirstUser`. login.ts (under the public prefix `/_emdash/api/auth/atproto/`) has no setup-state check. Trigger: the owner completes wizard step 1; an attacker POSTs `{handle:"attacker.bsky.social"}` to /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/login and completes OAuth. They become admin, finalizeSetup runs, and the owner's setup flow then fails with SETUP_COMPLETE.

Checking the setup_complete flag doesn't prevent concurrent first-user callbacks. Both can create admins, or the second DID can be auto-linked to the admin through the shared wizard email. callback.ts:126 says "Using an option flag instead of countUsers() avoids a TOCTOU race where two concurrent callbacks both see 0 users and both create admins". But the flag is read with `options.get("emdash:setup_complete")` and only written later by `finalizeSetup`, with no lock or conditional write in between. The core OAuth callback ([provider]/callback.ts:140) has the same comment and the same read-then-write pattern. The comment at line 147 even says "safe if two callbacks race past the check".

The atproto routes build client_id and redirect_uri from the internal request origin instead of the configured public origin, so atproto login breaks behind a TLS-terminating proxy. login.ts, setup-admin.ts:56 and callback.ts:42 all use `const baseUrl = url.origin;`. client-metadata.ts uses `new URL(request.url).origin`. Every core auth route in the diff was switched to `getPublicOrigin(url, emdash?.config)` for exactly this reverse-proxy case (see public-url.ts). Behind a proxy, `http://localhost:4321/_emdash/api/auth/atproto/callback` would be registered as the redirect_uri.

Astro's checkOrigin is turned off for the whole site, while EmDash's replacement CSRF check only covers its own public and plugin API routes. `const securityConfig = { checkOrigin: false, ... }; updateConfig({ security: securityConfig, ...})`. `checkPublicCsrf` is called only from middleware/auth.ts for `isPublicApiRoute` and `/_emdash/api/plugins/`. The other /_emdash routes need the X-EmDash-Request header. Template or user routes such as a contact-form POST no longer get any origin check. This weakens a secure default.

A plugin with allowedHosts "*" can fetch any host, including private IPs and metadata endpoints, with no SSRF validation. `isHostAllowed` gains `if (pattern === "*") return true;`. `createHttpAccess` only calls `isHostAllowed` and then `globalThis.fetch(currentUrl, ...)`. `createUnrestrictedHttpAccess` (the fetch:any path) calls `validateExternalUrl(currentUrl)` on every hop. Trigger: a plugin with `allowedHosts: ["*"]` calls `ctx.http.fetch("http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/")`, and the request goes through.

The atproto callback accepts any valid state/code without tying it to the browser that started the flow, which allows login CSRF. login.ts returns the authorize URL and sets no cookie or session marker. The OAuth state is held only server-side in the `auth:atproto` `states` collection (db-store.ts). callback.ts calls `client.callback(url.searchParams)` and then `session.set("user", { id: user.id })`, with no check that ties the state to the current session.

Changing Pages concurrency to cancel-in-progress: true lets a later push to main cancel a run that is already in its deploy job, and it is unplanned infra scope in a CSS theme change. The diff replaces `group: "pages"` / `cancel-in-progress: false` with `group: "pages-${{ github.ref }}"` / `cancel-in-progress: true`. The concurrency block is at workflow level (lines 25-27), so it covers the `deploy` job (`actions/deploy-pages@v4`, lines 57-70), which runs on every push to `refs/heads/main`. Two pushes to main in quick succession share the group `pages-refs/heads/main`, and the second cancels the first even while it is deploying. The old `false` value, GitHub's starter setting for Pages, let a running deployment finish and only skipped the queued runs in between. risk.json lists `infra` under `unplanned` with the match `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. Nothing else in the diff needs a workflow change: the rest is CSS.

Lazy key rotation in get() writes back with CAS (bumping the stored version) but returns the credential with its old version, so a following CAS write by the caller fails with VersionConflict and a CacheLayer above caches the stale version. `get()` calls `self.inner.put(updated, PutMode::CompareAndSwap { expected_version: credential.version })` and discards the `Ok(_)` result, then does `Ok(credential)` with the original `version`. `InMemoryStore::put` sets `credential.version = expected_version + 1` on CAS, so the stored version is one higher than the returned one. `CacheLayer::get` (cache.rs:149-150) caches whatever the inner `get` returns. The new test `lazy_reencryption_on_read_when_key_id_differs` only checks the raw envelope's `key_id`. It never checks the returned version or a follow-up CAS write.

with_keys() does not register the empty-string alias that new() adds for pre-rotation records, so records with key_id "" can't be decrypted after a move to with_keys; the crypto.rs doc says empty key IDs are rejected, which is the opposite of what new() does. `new()` does `keys.insert(String::new(), key); // alias for pre-rotation data` (line 69). `with_keys` only collects the supplied pairs, so `key_for_id("")` returns `StoreError::Backend("encryption key '' not found — cannot decrypt")`. `EncryptedData.key_id` is `#[serde(default)]`, so old envelopes deserialize with "". crypto.rs:80 says "The encryption layer rejects empty key IDs at runtime", but `new()` accepts them. The public `encrypt()`/`encrypt_with_aad()` also still produce `key_id: ""`, while `encrypt_with_key_id` rejects it.

The no-AAD decrypt fallback was removed with no migration path, and the locked baseline test legacy_data_without_aad_still_readable was rewritten as rejects_data_without_aad to assert the opposite. The old `decrypt_data` fell back to `crypto::decrypt(key, &encrypted)` when AAD decryption failed. The new `decrypt_possibly_rotating` only calls `decrypt_with_aad` and maps any failure to `StoreError::Backend`. The test `legacy_data_without_aad_still_readable` (which asserted `fetched.data == b"legacy-secret"`) was renamed to `rejects_data_without_aad` and now asserts `unwrap_err()`. The crypto.rs doc says "a migration must re-encrypt all records before upgrading", but the diff contains no migration tool or command.

The persisted state_kind strings and the basic-auth field name changed with no compatibility path, so existing stored records fail with KindMismatch or don't deserialize. `identity_state!(BearerToken, "bearer", 1)` and `identity_state!(BasicAuth, "basic_auth", 1)` became `identity_state!(SecretToken, "secret_token", 1)` and `identity_state!(IdentityPassword, "identity_password", 1)`. The resolver rejects with `if stored.state_kind != expected_kind` (resolver.rs:243). The removed `BasicAuth` had `pub username: String`; `IdentityPassword` has `identity: String`. The only CredentialStore backend in the repo is InMemoryStore, so the impact today is limited.

Plaintext leaves the Zeroizing wrapper into a plain Vec, and the rotation path clones the plaintext credential and drops the copy without zeroizing it. `credential.data = std::mem::take(&mut *plaintext);` moves the bytes out of the `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` into `StoredCredential.data`. Then `StoredCredential { data: re_encrypted, ..credential.clone() }` clones `credential`, so its plaintext `data` is copied and then dropped without zeroization.

After jumpToMessage loads an older window, a sent or received message is appended right after it. The new message becomes `$newest`, so the `canLoadNewer` exists-query finds nothing after it. The wait for media before pinning to the bottom was replaced by a fixed 220ms window, so media that loads later leaves the user scrolled above the latest message. x-init calls `scrollToBottom()` after 100ms and sets `initializing = false` after 220ms. `onAnyMediaLoad()` only re-scrolls to the bottom `if (this.initializing)`. The removed `waitForMedia()` resolved on every img/video load or error before `scrollToBottom(); booting = false;`.

A jump scroll cancels its own media re-centering lock. scrollToMessageCenterWithRetry() sets jumpTargetId and a 1200ms lock, then scrollToMessageCenter() assigns container.scrollTop without updating lastScrollTop. The resulting scroll event enters onScroll(); any movement over eight pixels clears jumpTargetId and jumpLockUntil. onAnyMediaLoad() therefore cannot recenter that target when media subsequently changes the layout.
